output.brief: The rise in VA-220 failures traces to Pellacott's 2026-built valves, not to installers or firmware. A quality-lab teardown found the slide seal deformed and unseated in 38 of 41 returned valves. A helium retest of unused warehouse stock found 11% of Pellacott 2026 valves leaking at the seat, against 1% for Pellacott 2025 valves and 0% for Durrant-Hale. Matched claim rates are the same across installer and firmware groups, so those two explanations don't hold. Pellacott's leak certificates do not reflect real testing. The test rig was out of service from 9 Jan 2026, no VA-220 test program was loaded on the other rigs, and the certificate tables repeat four sequences, including ones from Nov 2025. The SupplierPath score rose because it rewards submitted paperwork, so it gave Pellacott dock-to-stock status. Do not release the six held lots on new certificates, and do not penalise the installers. Quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and release only after Brenmoor's own helium testing. Press Pellacott for evidence of the claimed backup rig. Check other suppliers' records, since they are unverified. Whether the new Corlin seal or the Line 3 move is the cause is still open, so hold off on ordering a seal reversal until that is tested.
